If at least $k$ of its $\ell$ edges are faulty, some $k$-subset is entirely faulty. There are at most $\binom\ell k\le2^\ell$ such subsets; by [F4] each has probability $\epsilon^k\le\epsilon^{\ell/2}$ for $\epsilon\in[0,1]$. The union bound [F5] gives $\mathbb P(P\text{ is a failure witness})\le2^\ell\epsilon^{\ell/2}$.

There are at most $(d+1)3^\ell$ candidate paths of length $\ell$ by [F3]. By [F2], every logical failure lies in the union of witness events for paths with $d\le\ell\le n$. The finite union bound [F5] and step 1.1 therefore give $P_{\mathrm{logical}}\le\sum_{\ell=d}^{n}(d+1)3^\ell 2^\ell\epsilon^{\ell/2}=(d+1)\sum_{\ell=d}^{n}(36\epsilon)^{\ell/2}$.

If $\epsilon<1/36$, set $r=6\sqrt{\epsilon}<1$. The finite sum is at most $\sum_{\ell=d}^{\infty}r^\ell=r^d/(1-r)$, so $P_{\mathrm{logical}}\le\frac{d+1}{1-6\sqrt{\epsilon}}(6\sqrt{\epsilon})^d$. The denominator is a fixed positive constant for fixed $\epsilon<1/36$, while $d+1$ is polynomial in $d$; hence the bound decays exponentially up to a polynomial prefactor.

Let $C$ be a finite channel-location schedule as in [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]], with finite ordered location set $L(C)$. A location is a supplied gate, preparation, measurement, reset, or explicitly scheduled idle channel with declared support $S_\ell$. The model does not create idle locations that the schedule did not declare.

Fix $\eta\in[0,1]$. A fault pattern is a subset $F\subseteq L(C)$. Its probability is
$$
\mathbb P(F)=\eta^{|F|}(1-\eta)^{|L(C)\setminus F|},
$$
where integer powers use the empty-product convention $x^0=1$, including at $x=0$. Thus each location faults with probability $\eta$, and the event classes generated by the fault/no-fault indicator at each location form an independent family in the sense of [[def-independent-families-of-event-classes]]. Conditional on $F$, each $\ell\in F$ replaces only the ideal operation at $\ell$ by an arbitrary CPTP map supported on $S_\ell$; all other locations apply their ideal channels. A replacement map may depend on the full pattern, but it acts only at its own location. Faults at measurement and reset locations are represented by channels on their declared quantum and classical registers.

This definition is the independent, local fault model: location indicators are independent, and each fault map acts at its own scheduled location.

In the independent local fault model, events determined by pairwise disjoint finite sets of location fault indicators are mutually independent. In particular, bad-rectangle events determined only by the faults in pairwise disjoint child rectangles are independent.

derivations.claim: Inductively suppose every level-$r$ complete or truncated witness has bad probability at most $p_r$. A bad level-$(r+1)$ root has an all-bad pair among at most $A_1$ fixed candidate pairs by [A1]. Each pair's events are determined by fixed disjoint location sets, so [F1] and [F2] bound their intersection probability by $p_r^2$. Applying [F3] proves the bound $A_1p_r^2=p_{r+1}$. The base bound is $p_0=\eta$.

The envelope has $p_0=\eta=A_1^{-1}(A_1\eta)$. If $p_r=A_1^{-1}(A_1\eta)^{2^r}$, its recurrence gives $p_{r+1}=A_1(A_1^{-1}(A_1\eta)^{2^r})^2=A_1^{-1}(A_1\eta)^{2^{r+1}}$. Thus the closed form holds at every level.

By [F3], the probability $\alpha$ of any bad top-level root is at most $Np_r$. By [A1], the conditional output law on its complement is ideal. Thus the full output law is $(1-\alpha)P_{\rm ideal}+\alpha Q$ for some probability law $Q$; at $\alpha=0$ choose $Q$ arbitrarily. Each success probability differs from ideal by at most $\alpha\le Np_r$.

If $\eta=0$, $p_r=0$ at every level. Otherwise for fixed $\eta<1/A_1$ put $\theta=A_1\eta\in(0,1)$ and $c=-\log\theta>0$. The bound $Np_r\le\delta$ holds whenever $2^r\ge c^{-1}\log(N/(A_1\delta))$, and level zero suffices when the right side is at most one. Hence the least qualifying level is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$. The finite recursive gadget family has a constant size and depth expansion bound $\kappa\ge1$, so a circuit of original size $S$ and depth $D$ has size at most $S\kappa^r$ and depth at most $D\kappa^r$, with a fixed boundary factor. Thus its multiplicative overheads are polylogarithmic. Also $p_r=A_1^{-1}e^{-c2^r}\to0$ super-exponentially.

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to each level-$r$ rectangle. Its proof counts fault-witness sets and uses only the local-stochastic subset bound, so it requires no independence between child fault indicators. Thus each top-level circuit rectangle is bad with probability at most $p_r=A^{-1/q}(A^{1/q}\eta)^{(q+1)^r}$.

If $\eta=0$, each single-location fault event has probability zero by the local-stochastic subset bound; the finite union bound gives no faults almost surely, so level zero suffices. Otherwise put $\theta=A^{1/q}\eta\in(0,1)$ and $c=-\log\theta>0$. Any $r$ with $(q+1)^r\ge c^{-1}\log(NA^{-1/q}/\delta)$ is sufficient; if the logarithm is nonpositive or its positive value is at most $c$, $r=0$ suffices. For fixed parameters, the least qualifying $r$ is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ as $N/\delta\to\infty$.

By [F11], the probability $\alpha$ that at least one of the $N$ top-level circuit rectangles is bad satisfies $\alpha\le Np_r$. For every fault pattern, [F9] gives a conditional channel, so its output on the fixed joint data input and external reference is a density operator. On the complementary event, recursive goodness gives at most $q$ bad children in every stage. The contract [F8] and sparse-path correction guarantee [F4] make each corrected logical stage ideal for the per-location channels allowed by [F1]. Thus every pattern with no bad top-level rectangle outputs $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}$. If $\alpha>0$, the normalized finite mixture of bad-pattern outputs is a density operator $\tau$; if $\alpha=0$, choose any density operator for $\tau$. Then $\rho_{\mathrm{out}}=(1-\alpha)\rho_{\mathrm{id}}+\alpha\tau$, and [F10] confirms that the weighted schedule output is a channel.

By homogeneity of trace distance and [F6], $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})=\alpha D(\tau,\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le\alpha\le Np_r$. Applying [F7] to the final POVM bounds its output total-variation distance by $Np_r$, and every success event changes by at most that total-variation distance.

Because the gadget family is fixed and finite, choose a constant $\kappa\ge1$ bounding both the number of elementary locations and the scheduled depth of every replacement gadget, including preparation, control, reset, and idle locations. Replacing each location of a schedule of size $S$ and depth $D$ gives size at most $S\kappa$ and depth at most $D\kappa$: replace disjoint locations of each original layer in parallel and pad their gadgets to the common depth bound. Induction gives size at most $S\kappa^r$ and depth at most $D\kappa^r$ at level $r$. Thus the multiplicative size and depth overheads are at most $\kappa^r$, which is a fixed power of $\log(N/\delta)$ by step 1.2.

citations.quote:
Let $C_2\subseteq C_1\le\mathbb F_2^n$, $n\ge1$, and
$k=\dim C_1-\dim C_2$. The coset vectors from
[[def-qc-css-code-from-nested-binary-codes]] define an isometric encoding of
$k$ logical qubits. For every $c\in C_2$ and $h\in C_1^\perp$, $X^c$ and
$Z^h$ commute, and each fixes every encoded coset vector. Their common
$+1$ eigenspace is exactly this encoding. The conclusion requires only
$C_2\subseteq C_1$; it does not require
$C_2^\perp\subseteq C_1$.

Moreover, for every $x\in C_1$, the Hadamard transform is

$$H^{\otimes n}|x+C_2\rangle=2^{-k/2}\sum_{y+C_1^\perp\in C_2^\perp/C_1^\perp}(-1)^{x\cdot y}|y+C_1^\perp\rangle.$$

The phase is independent of the representatives $x+C_2$ and
$y+C_1^\perp$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be an abelian group of Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators with
$-I\notin S$, generated by $r$ independent checks. Then

$$P_S:=|S|^{-1}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

is the orthogonal projector onto the stabilizer code space and has rank
$2^{n-r}$. In particular, the code space is nonzero, including when $r=n$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits whose code space has dimension
$2^k$. The stabilizer **distance** is

$$d(S):=\min\{\operatorname{wt}(E):E\in N(S)\setminus Z_nS\}\quad\text{if }k>0.$$

This is a set difference: it excludes scalar-phase multiples of stabilizers.
If $k=0$, define $d(S)=+\infty$, since there is no nontrivial logical Pauli
class.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits of distance $d(S)$. Every Pauli error $E$ of
weight less than $d(S)$ either acts as a scalar on the code space (when
$E\in Z_nS$) or is detected by some stabilizer check. A finite error channel
whose Kraus operators lie in the span of Pauli operators of weight at most
$t$, for $t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, is correctable whenever $2t<d(S)$. In particular, all unknown Pauli
errors of weight at most $t$ are correctable.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

Consider one block of $m$ tensor factors $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_m$, its code subspace $Q$, and an arbitrary finite reference system $R$. For an integer $s\ge0$, let $\mathcal E_s$ be the complex linear span of all operators on the block supported on at most $s$ physical coordinates, with support and weight as in [[def-qc-local-operator-support-and-weight]].

A density operator $\rho$ on the block and $R$ is $s$-deviated from a code-supported density operator $\sigma$ if there is a CPTP map $\mathcal N$ on the block with a finite Kraus family $K_1,\ldots,K_t\in\mathcal E_s$ such that $\rho=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^t(K_j\otimes I_R)\sigma(K_j^\dagger\otimes I_R)$ and $\sum_{j=1}^tK_j^\dagger K_j=I$.
Here $\sigma$ is **code-supported** when its joint support is contained in $Q\otimes R$. The reference factor is retained in the identity above. Equality of reduced states outside a coordinate set is not the definition of deviation here.

For a finite family of live blocks indexed by $B$, use the joint error space $\mathcal E_s^{B}:=\operatorname{span}\{\bigotimes_{b\in B}A_b: A_b\text{ is supported on at most }s\text{ coordinates of block }b\}$. Joint $s$-deviation means the same Kraus formula with a single CPTP map on all live blocks, every Kraus operator in $\mathcal E_s^B$, and identity on the external reference alone. The ideal joint state is supported in $\bigotimes_{b\in B}Q_b\otimes R$. This includes the original one-block definition when $|B|=1$. The joint error map need not factor across blocks: a faulty multi-block gate can correlate their errors. Other live data blocks are part of the data system, not part of the unchanged external reference. Statements about deviation per block in a multi-block computation use this joint convention.

For an integer $\ell\ge1$, **literal support-propagation spread** applies to a specified unitary circuit segment: conjugating a fault operator supported on $S$ through the remaining fault-free unitary gates produces an operator supported on at most $\ell|S|$ output coordinates per block. For several faults, expand the finite Kraus families and take the union of their propagated supports. This gives the sum of the individual support bounds. The bound must account for all input blocks of a multi-block gate.

For a correcting, preparing or measuring gadget, an **effective spread budget** is instead part of an explicit input-sector/output-sector contract. The gadget declares its admitted joint error sectors, allowed fault supports, ideal logical channel or instrument, and joint residual-error sector for each allowed fault count. The required identities compare its decoded output with that ideal logical channel or instrument on every admitted input, with an arbitrary finite external reference. Measurement identities are identities of the subnormalized branch maps, not equations obtained by ignoring their probabilities. Any auxiliary fault memory is retained in the description of the faulty maps and may change there; it is distinct from the untouched external reference, and nonfaulty locations leave that memory alone. An identity that retains fault memory must specify its output memory action rather than silently identify it with the reference identity.

The numerical computation and correction budgets needed for sparse induction are explicitly imposed in the separately stated proper-code gadget contract; the word spread alone supplies none of those identities. In particular, incoming-error propagation and the full noisy correction action must be checked. Zero-fault recovery on arbitrary inputs remains a separate requirement. No global equation moving arbitrary input faults through a recovery channel on its whole input space is asserted.

derivations.claim: The columns of $B$ are the seven distinct nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^3$, and its last three columns are the standard basis, so its rank is three. Each row has weight four and any two distinct rows have overlap two; hence $BB^{\mathsf T}=0$ and $D\subseteq D^\perp$. Every nonzero word of $D$ evaluates a nonzero linear functional on these seven columns. Such a functional takes value one on four of the eight vectors of $\mathbb F_2^3$, and takes value zero on the zero vector, so all seven nonzero words of $D$ have weight four. Also $Bx^{\mathsf T}=0$ and $\operatorname{wt}(x)=3$, so $x\in D^\perp\setminus D$. Since $\dim D^\perp=4$, it follows that $D^\perp=D\sqcup(x+D)$. The two coset sums defining $V$ are orthonormal.

The six checks $X^b,Z^b$, with $b$ ranging over the rows of $B$, are independent commuting Hermitian Paulis, and their common fixed space is $\operatorname{im}V$ by [F1]. A Pauli $i^kX^uZ^v$ centralizes them exactly when $u,v\in D^\perp$, and is a scalar-phase stabilizer exactly when $u,v\in D$. No nonzero word of $D^\perp=\ker B$ has weight one or two, since the columns of $B$ are nonzero and distinct. Thus a nontrivial centralizer class has weight at least three. The operators $X^x,Z^x$ attain three and act respectively as logical $X,Z$ on the displayed basis: translation by $x$ exchanges the cosets, and $x\cdot(ax+c)=a$ since $x\cdot x=1$ and $x\perp D$. Therefore this seven-qubit code has distance exactly three.

Partition the $49$ coordinates into seven ordered inner blocks. Take the six inner checks from step 1.2 in each block, giving $42$ checks. Lift the six outer checks by replacing their single-qubit $X,Z$ factors with the inner representatives $X^x,Z^x$. All $48$ checks commute: inner checks commute with these representatives, and the representatives obey exactly the one-qubit Pauli commutation rule on each block because $x\cdot x=1$. The checks are independent. Indeed, reducing a relation among them modulo the seven inner stabilizer groups leaves a relation among the six independent outer Pauli labels; thus all six outer exponents vanish, and independence of the disjoint inner checks then makes the remaining $42$ exponents vanish. They fix every vector in $\operatorname{im}W$, so their group excludes $-I$. By [F2] their fixed space has dimension $2^{49-48}=2$ and consequently equals $\operatorname{im}W$.

Let $E$ centralize these $48$ checks. Its restriction to each inner block centralizes the six inner checks. Modulo an inner stabilizer and scalar phase, that restriction is uniquely one of $I,X^x,Z^x,X^xZ^x$, by the description $D^\perp/D$ in steps 1.1–1.2. Its seven labels therefore define an outer Pauli. Commutation with the lifted outer checks says exactly that this outer Pauli centralizes the seven-qubit outer code. If its outer class is trivial, multiplying the corresponding lifted outer stabilizers leaves an inner stabilizer in each block; hence $E$ is a scalar-phase stabilizer of the $49$-qubit code. Otherwise at least three inner blocks have nontrivial labels by step 1.2, and each of those restrictions has weight at least three. Thus every nontrivial class has weight at least nine. Lift the weight-three outer logical $X^x$ using weight-three inner $X^x$ in its three occupied blocks. This gives a nontrivial logical Pauli of weight nine. The distance is therefore exactly nine.

Let $E_1,\ldots,E_M$ list all phase-free Paulis of weight at most four. Their normalized Kraus family $E_a/\sqrt M$ defines a channel, since each $E_a$ is unitary. Apply [F4] with $t=4$, since $2t=8<9$, and compose its recovery with inverse encoding to obtain a decoded recovery $\mathcal R$ with Kraus operators $R_j$. This one recovery works uniformly on the entire error span. Indeed its correction of the displayed mixed-Pauli channel means that the operators $R_jE_aW/\sqrt M$ are Kraus operators of the identity logical channel. Each must be a scalar multiple of the logical identity: for every pure logical input their output vectors must lie in its one-dimensional span, since their positive rank-one output sum is that pure input; applying this to a basis and its pairwise sums makes the scalar independent of the input. Thus $R_jE_aW=c_{ja}I_L$. For any channel with Kraus operators $K_h=\sum_a\alpha_{ha}E_a$, it follows that $R_jK_hW=(\sum_a\alpha_{ha}c_{ja})I_L$; trace preservation makes the sum of squared scalar moduli one. Therefore the decoded channel is the identity, also after tensoring every operator with $I_R$. This proves uniform capacity four and hence the declared smaller capacity two.

Since $D^\perp/D$ has representatives $0,x$, $x\cdot x=1$, and $D=(D^\perp)^\perp$, the exact Hadamard formula in [F1] gives $H^{\otimes7}V=VH$. For $c\in D$, its weight is zero or four, so $i^{\operatorname{wt}(c)}=1$. For $x+c$, the weight identity $\operatorname{wt}(x+c)=\operatorname{wt}(x)+\operatorname{wt}(c)-2|\operatorname{supp}(x)\cap\operatorname{supp}(c)|$ is congruent to three modulo four: the first weight is three, the second is divisible by four, and the intersection size is even because $x\perp D$. Thus $S^{\otimes7}V=VS^\dagger$, with no additional scalar phase. Taking adjoints of this diagonal action also gives $(S^\dagger)^{\otimes7}V=VS$.

On the pair of encoded computational basis states with logical bits $a,b$, coordinatewise CNOT sends the summand $|ax+c\rangle|bx+e\rangle$ to $|ax+c\rangle|(a+b)x+c+e\rangle$. The substitution $(c,e)\mapsto(c,c+e)$ is a bijection of $D\times D$, so the transformed sum is exactly $V|a\rangle\otimes V|a+b\rangle$. Linearity gives the seven-coordinate CNOT intertwining identity. Applying it first in every inner block pair and then to the outer encoding proves the stated $49$-coordinate identity. Likewise step 3.1 at the inner and outer levels gives $H^{\otimes49}W=WH$ and $S^{\otimes49}W=V^{\otimes7}(S^\dagger)^{\otimes7}V=WS$.

Each circuit consists of $49$ disjoint one- or two-qubit gates in one layer, so its size is $49$ and its depth is one. In a CNOT layer a location touches one coordinate in each block; in a one-block layer it touches one coordinate. Replacing any chosen locations by an arbitrary joint CPTP map supported on their union changes no other output coordinate, since all other gates are disjoint from that union. The same support assertion holds for every Kraus operator, including after tensoring $I_R$; no product assumption on the joint fault map is used. Thus one faulty location has spread at most one per block, and any collection has the union bound in [F6]. Conjugating an input-supported operator by a transversal layer also preserves coordinate labels, except that CNOT may transfer its support to the matching coordinate of the other block. Input supports $A,B$ therefore give output supports contained in $A\cup B$ in each block. This proves all gate and spread assertions.

Let $C$ be a finite channel-location schedule as in [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]], with finite ordered location set $L(C)$. A location is a supplied gate, preparation, measurement, reset, or explicitly scheduled idle channel with declared support $S_\ell$. The model does not create idle locations that the schedule did not declare.

Fix $\eta\in[0,1]$. A fault pattern is a subset $F\subseteq L(C)$. Its probability is
$$
\mathbb P(F)=\eta^{|F|}(1-\eta)^{|L(C)\setminus F|},
$$
where integer powers use the empty-product convention $x^0=1$, including at $x=0$. Thus each location faults with probability $\eta$, and the event classes generated by the fault/no-fault indicator at each location form an independent family in the sense of [[def-independent-families-of-event-classes]]. Conditional on $F$, each $\ell\in F$ replaces only the ideal operation at $\ell$ by an arbitrary CPTP map supported on $S_\ell$; all other locations apply their ideal channels. A replacement map may depend on the full pattern, but it acts only at its own location. Faults at measurement and reset locations are represented by channels on their declared quantum and classical registers.

This definition is the independent, local fault model: location indicators are independent, and each fault map acts at its own scheduled location.

For every finite family of events $A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1}$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i<n}A_i\right)\le\sum_{i<n}\mathbb P(A_i).$$
For $n=0$ both sides are $0$.
